segments.buyers: AI cloud providers ('neoclouds'), AI labs, large companies and governments.
pos: The growth engine: AI servers +100% and traditional servers +122% in the July quarter vs a year earlier.
Backed by a $95bn AI order backlog (1 Sep 2026), about two quarters of total company revenue.
ISG's operating margin rose to 15.0% from 8.8% a year earlier as volume grew.
neg: Not recurring: big, lumpy deals that can slip between quarters.
Concentrated in a small number of very large AI buyers whose funding depends on debt markets (chain C2).
Depends on Nvidia's GPU supply and memory prices (chains C1, C5).

segments.name: Storage
segments.sells: Data storage systems (all-flash arrays, file and object storage).
segments.buyers: Companies and governments; increasingly for AI data.
pos: Usually one of Dell's higher-margin hardware lines (Dell does not report storage margin separately), so growth here helps profit more than its size suggests.
+26% in the July quarter vs a year earlier, after −1% in the Oct 2025 quarter.
neg: Shrinking share: 11.9% of revenue over the last 4 quarters vs 16.3% a year earlier, as servers grow faster.

segments.name: Commercial PCs
segments.sells: PCs, laptops and monitors for businesses.
pos: Growing again: +22% in the July quarter vs a year earlier (PC upgrade cycle).
A steady, diversified customer base that does not depend on AI.
neg: Low margin: CSG earns about 6.6% operating margin (last 4 quarters) vs ISG's 13.2%.
Memory price rises force PC price increases that can dent demand (chain C1).

segments.name: Consumer PCs
segments.sells: PCs and laptops for consumers (incl. Alienware gaming).
pos: Small (about 4% of revenue), so swings matter little.
+7% in the July quarter vs a year earlier.
neg: Long decline: share of revenue fell from about 10% to under 5% in 3 years.
Most price-sensitive part of Dell; memory-driven price rises hit it first.

pos: The shift in mix alone added 0.8 pts to segment operating margin vs a year earlier (last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters a year earlier, each part's margin held at that earlier level).
The shift in mix alone added 1.1 pts to segment operating margin vs 3 years earlier (last 4 quarters vs the 4 quarters 3 years earlier, each part's margin held at that earlier level).
neg: Partly recurring revenue (long-life contracts or design wins) down 7 pts in 3 years to 12% of sales (last 4 quarters).
Concentration: Servers & networking (incl. AI servers) is 51% of sales (last 4 quarters).

shift.title: What the shift means for Dell
pos: Servers (mostly AI) rose from 20% of revenue (4 quarters to Jan 2024) to 51% (4 quarters to Jul 2026; 57% in the July 2026 quarter alone), turning Dell from a PC company into an AI infrastructure company.
Profit followed: operating profit $5.4bn in the July quarter vs $1.8bn a year earlier (SEC); ISG margin rose with scale.
neg: Lower-margin mix: AI servers earn less per dollar than storage and services, so company gross margin is structurally lower than before (20.0% in FY26 vs 23.8% in FY24, SEC).
More concentrated and more cyclical: a pause in AI spending would hit a much larger share of Dell's revenue than before.

mix.note: Segment operating margin = the segment's operating profit ÷ its revenue, before costs Dell does not allocate (mainly amortisation of purchase intangibles, share-based pay and other corporate costs). Dell reports profit only for ISG and CSG, so servers and storage share ISG's margin, and commercial and consumer PCs share CSG's.
checks: Reported parts miss the total by up to 6.7% of revenue: shown as Other.

bubble.history: Back-checked on monthly data 1998-2026: Breaking first fired in Aug 2000, Oct 2007 and Mar 2022, each within 0-5 months of the market top and before most of the fall (S&P 500 then fell a further 40%, 53% and 21%). False alarms: Aug 2011, Nov 2018 and Mar 2023, after which the S&P 500 was 14-28% higher a year later. It confirms a top is probably in; it does not call it in advance.
